profile.headline: Senior Embedded Software Engineer at Apple
profile.summary:
THE PAST 
When I graduated from the University of Oregon with a degree in Journalism and Advertising, like most college grads, I was tired of being broke. Instead of pursuing my passions or following my degree, I found a job as quickly as I could. It was a job as - wait for it... an insurance salesman! Obviously a job where I could utilize my skills, right!? 

The catch 22: I hated the job but, I learned some valuable skills. And, most importantly it guided me here. It didn't take me long to realize that when you spend 40 hours a week doing something, you better LIKE doing it. With that, and many sparing details, I quit and went back to school. I now have a M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering and I LOVE what I do.

THE PRESENT 
After more than 10 years in the industry, not much has changed - I still love what I do! The best part of embedded software is being able to build something you can touch and interact with. Nonetheless, I’m excited to learn anything software related. I’ve spent at least some portion of all of my positions developing on Android, in particular for internet of things (IOT). I’m always looking for ways to increase efficiency like automating repetitive tasks using Python. I pride myself in code readability and organization. In a world where documentation is often an afterthought and “just making it work” is usually where the buck stops, there is something cathartic about writing clear and organized code that includes documentation that truly makes me feel “finished”. 

THE FUTURE 
No matter how cool the product (or boring) it’s the people and culture that make it exciting. Yeah, it may sound cliché, but it’s true and it’s one of my top things to look for in a new adventure. Speaking of adventure, for the right opportunity, I am available to relocate. My family loves new experiences, but we do have kids that won’t love being too far from grandma and grandpa, so east coast/midwest doesn’t work right now. My interests are wide. I’ve found that this industry has many unique and interesting problems to solve that you’d never think of. Nonetheless some of my interests are: EVs, robotics, automation, arts and storytelling, and space.

positions.title: Product Development Engineer
positions.description:
Cinder Labs began as a support team within, at the time, our parent company, Allion USA – a consumer electronics testing house. We developed anything to support Allion. That included simple scripts, full-blown software tools, and in the best cases (my best cases) robotics. Some of those items became sellable products. See for yourself: http://cindersolutions.com/labs/. I had a hand in most of those items. Since then, we became a sister company to Allion – separate but affiliated. We continue to work on our own products, but the growing bulk of our business is consulting work and product development for 3rd parties.

My role within Cinder has varied over the years, as with any small company, you wear many hats. I began my career as a digital designer. I designed schematics, printed circuit boards, selected parts, assembled products, and worked with manufacturers to get our stuff built. There is a satisfaction about building anything from the ground up that I can’t describe, but I realized my real excitement was in programming the electronics rather than building them. I now spend most of my time developing firmware and software around IoT. That includes both the embedded side firmware(C) and Android mobile development(Java). Of course you can't forget data analysis to verify our designs, for that I mostly use Python. 

Highlights:
	Created Minimal Viable Product BLE gaming device for first round funding 
        Competitive device analysis and testing with national Interlock company
	Worked with Trinity VR in developing a virtual Reality game controller
	Automated/programmable USB 2.0 Compliant testing hub developed for Lab126 (Amazon)
